clue.text: Heading for sultanate, linger behind guide

parts.note: to linger behind is to drag, to trail along slowly
Oman is the sultanate on the Arabian peninsula; the word heading for it goes in front

explanation.surface: Someone loiters at the back while making for a Gulf state, apparently in need of a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for 'linger behind' is the heading placed before the sultanate. A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman is an interpreter who acted as a guide for travellers in the Middle East.

clue.text: Predatory nature of soldiers quick about it

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a standard abbreviation for soldiers

indicators.note: the word for quick goes about, around, the word it

parts.note: pacy means quick, fast-moving
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that greedy soldiers are quick to get their hands on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is greed and the urge to seize, the essence of a predatory character.

clue.text: Recipient of confidences got tapes mixed up

indicators.note: mixed up says the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trusted with secrets has got their recordings in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the phrase 'between you, me and the gatepost', said when sharing a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'between you, me and the gatepost' makes the post the silent sharer of a confidence.

clue.text: Letters man read out

indicators.note: read out means said aloud, so the word is matched with one that sounds the same

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A man reads out his correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Post consists of letters, and mail is the collective word for it.

clue.text: There shouldn't be any objection to a news broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered widely, so these letters are sent in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nobody ought to complain about a news programme going out.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'broadcast' scrambles TO, A and NEWS together; 'broadcast' looks like a description of the news.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase means no problem at all, a reassurance that nothing stands in the way.

clue.text: Angry wife-murderer and forger

parts.note: a black mood or black look is an angry one
George Joseph Smith was the notorious 'Brides in the Bath' murderer who drowned his wives

explanation.surface: A list of three characters: an angry man, a killer of his wife, and a counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: SMITH refers to George Joseph Smith, hanged in 1915 for the 'Brides in the Bath' murders of women he had married. 'Forger' is one who works metal at a forge, not a counterfeiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith works iron at a forge, so he literally forges metal.

clue.text: File almost out of date — that's nonsense!

parts.note: a folder is a file for holding papers

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: old means out of date

explanation.surface: Someone finds their file nearly obsolete and dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Folderol is foolish talk or trivial fuss, a word for silly nonsense.

clue.text: Sitting duck provides simple fare

definitions.meaning: a sitting duck is an easy target, someone easily beaten or exploited
read literally, food that is easy, uncomplicated to eat

explanation.surface: An easy target is said to supply plain food.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy meat is slang for a pushover; read literally it is meat that is simple to deal with.

clue.text: Show state of America

definitions.meaning: a stage show, the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical
one of the fifty United States, in the south-central region

explanation.surface: A display of something belonging to the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a famous Broadway musical named after the US state it is set in.

clue.text: Away from servants, family puts off condescending manner

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong or out of order, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: airs, as in putting on airs, are a superior, condescending manner

explanation.surface: Kept apart from the staff, the family drops its haughty attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles PUTS into UPST. In a grand household, as in the TV drama Upstairs, Downstairs, the family lived upstairs and the servants below.
explanation.definitionFit: In a country house the family's quarters were above the servants' hall, so the upper floors stand for the family.

clue.text: Terribly shifty about shuffling deck .

indicators.note: the word for shifty goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: wily means crafty, shifty

indicators.note: shuffling a deck mixes it, so the letters of the word are mixed

explanation.surface: A card sharp shuffles the deck in a terribly devious way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffling' reads as what a card player does to the deck, but it is the anagram signal; 'Terribly' is the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedly can be an intensifier meaning extremely or terribly, as in wickedly expensive.

clue.text: They provide close-up of jovial judge lost amongst wine containers

indicators.note: amongst places one piece within the other

parts.note: wine bins are racks or containers for storing bottles

indicators.note: lost means removed, so that letter goes missing

parts.note: jocular means jovial, jokey

explanation.surface: A cheerful magistrate goes missing among the wine racks, and something gives a close-up view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes the judge's letter from the word for jovial, and 'amongst' places what is left within the wine containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Binoculars magnify distant things so they appear close up, a fresh way to describe field glasses.

clue.text: At university in S. American city, rower finds America extremely funny

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city
an oar is a rower, someone who rows in a crew
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A student in Rio meets a rower who finds the United States a great laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is a British usage, as in 'up at Cambridge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uproarious means so funny that it provokes loud laughter.

clue.text: Deliver without charge

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to release or set at liberty

explanation.surface: A promise of delivery at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To free is to deliver from captivity, and free also means costing nothing.

clue.text: Play featuring Mary, heartless queen imprisoned in hovel

indicators.note: heartless removes the inner letters, keeping just the first and last of the name
imprisoned in says one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a filthy hovel
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A drama about Mary, a cruel queen locked up in a squalid hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mary, heartless queen' suggests Mary Queen of Scots, but heartless only trims Mary, and the queen is the usual abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystery plays were medieval dramas on Bible stories, so a mystery is a kind of play.

clue.text: Article sustains damage to fastener: 'maybe it's icing over

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath the others

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
a zip is a fastener on clothes
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing endures a broken zip; perhaps there's frosting on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'sustains' puts AN at the bottom, holding up MAR and ZIP. The definition says icing may go over it, as it does on a Christmas cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is the almond paste layer that icing is laid over on a fruit cake.

clue.text: Appeal for help carrying packing case for philosopher

indicators.note: carrying means holding one piece within the other

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, an appeal for help
a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: A call for help as someone lugs a crate for a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the ancient Athenian philosopher, teacher of Plato.

clue.text: One-time garment worn by men

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: An item of clothing that men used to wear in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' looks like 'former', but it splits into One and time.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, an undergarment or sports top worn by men.

clue.text: Start to get a modest sort of illumination

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: slight means modest, small in degree

explanation.surface: Advice to obtain a dim kind of lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaslight is lighting produced by burning gas in lamps, a type of illumination.

clue.text: Provincial city, or London suburb

definitions.meaning: the capital of the Canadian province of Alberta
a district in the north London borough of Enfield

explanation.surface: Choosing between a city in the provinces and a suburb of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is both the capital of Alberta and a district of north London.

clue.text: Soft soap — it comes in handy for washing

definitions.text: it comes in handy for washing
definitions.meaning: a face cloth held in the hand for washing

explanation.surface: A remark that a gentle soap is useful for a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' seems a washing product, but here it means flattery, and 'in handy' hints at a cloth held in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for flattering, evasive talk and also a face cloth used for washing.

clue.text: Sweet music

definitions.meaning: a hard stick-shaped confection sold at British seaside resorts
the genre of popular music with a strong beat

explanation.surface: Lovely music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is both a hard seaside confection and a style of popular music.

clue.text: Identical, notwithstanding

explanation.surface: Something exactly alike, even so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both completely identical and nevertheless, as in 'thanks all the same'.

clue.text: Doing something or nothing, depending on the space

definitions.text: Doing something or nothing, depending on the space

parts.words: Doing something or nothing, depending on the space
parts.note: written as two words the phrase means busy and active; closed up with no space it means idleness

explanation.surface: Whether one is active or idle depends on how much room there is.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'space' is the gap between letters, not room: with it the entry means active, without it doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two words it means busy at work; run together it means lack of activity.

clue.text: Cell only visible under microscope originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A cell that can be seen only through a microscope.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is an egg cell, the female reproductive cell.

clue.text: Drive a vintage float around

indicators.note: letters that float around drift out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Take an old car out, or a vintage float around.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'float around' shuffles A and VINTAGE; 'Drive' tempts toward cars, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate a vehicle is to steer or direct it, so it can mean to drive.

clue.text: Gap made by copyist? Possibly true

parts.note: an aper is one who apes, a copyist or mimic

indicators.note: possibly means the word may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A gap created by an imitator, which may well be real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns TRUE into TURE. APER is a crossword word for one who apes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening or gap, such as the hole that lets light into a camera.

clue.text: Checking one college set among the heather

indicators.note: set among places one piece inside the other

parts.note: ling is the common heather
I is the roman numeral one
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Inspecting a college built among moorland heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling, common heather, grows on British moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Limiting means restricting, holding something in check.
